projects.project_desc:
Hi Sefaria Engineering Team,
I built TzadekAI (https://tzadek.ai), a halachic Q&A app that uses your datasets to consult five "rabbi agents" from different eras of Jewish history (Geonim through Contemporary poskim). The goal was to be able to simulate if the rabbi agents from across time could come to consensus on various issues, or if there would tend to be disagreements. Comparing the contemporary to Geonim on its own has been an interesting exercise.

The project uses the Sefaria linker API in its execution to extract citations. I also used Sefaria/links and Sefaria/hebrew_library to build a local knowledge graph with ~918K texts and ~3.7M citation links and with OpenAI embeddings for semantic search across the corpus.

Each rabbi agent searches for era-appropriate sources using the knowledge graph, then Claude generates responses in that era's halachic style. A synthesis step analyzes consensus and provides a final ruling with sources linked back to Sefaria.

Trmnl is an e-paper display meant for passively displaying data from the internet, refreshing on its own throughout the day with a battery that lasts for months. Daily Torah Study is a plugin for the Trmnl which uses the Calendars API to present the Torah study schedule every day. This allows students of Torah to easily keep up to date on their daily study, using e-paper technology, which is distraction free and very suitable for shabbat.

projects.project_desc:
A couple of weeks ago, while visiting another college, a student gave over a chabura after shul on Shabbos morning. At first, the shiur began as normal, focusing on Yitzhak and laughter. As we approached the third or fourth text, something was off; the Hebrew text felt like a weird translation of an English text. The chabura was a success, but after I approached the student teaching, they admitted to using AI to help them with their chabura.

The night before, as a student was giving a short vort after Maariv, he notes that he couldn't quite find sources that argued his point, so he turned to "Rav Chat" for support.

These experiences showed me that people are already turning to Generative AI to create source sheets. That's why I built Darshan AI, a platform that can build out an entire source sheet with just a few clicks, and will cite sources back to Sefaria so that educators can confirm accuracy.

The acclaimed Dvar Torah feature instantly generates source-based talks tailored by difficulty, length, and occasion—ready for synagogue or home use. 

GoTorah bridges tradition and technology, empowering all learners to engage and share Torah in new, transformative ways.

projects.project_desc:
I have created a novel visualization of data provided by Sefaria. I created 5 interactive visualizations to show interesting information about Jewish scholars commentaries on the Babylonian Talmud. These include:

1. Visualization of scholars by their commentary approach based on breadth vs. depth which maps 47 scholars across four distinct archetypes

2. Pie charts show the distribution of scholars across archetypes and historical periods, providing quantitative insight into scholarly patterns

3. Bar graph comparing commentary distribution between Rishonim and Acharonim periods across the six orders (Sedarim), revealing how scholarly priorities shifted over time from practical law to theoretical discussions.

4. Statistical analysis comparing average commentary length between historical periods, revealing trends in scholarly writing style and the evolution from concise glosses to elaborate explanations.

5. A scatterplot which identifies tractates that generated disproportionate commentary; measures commentary density relative to tractate length (in dapim/folios), highlighting which topics were most "conversation-worthy" and generated intense scholarly discussion.


Non-interactive image versions of these visualizations can be scene in the projects GitHub readme. I hope to work on creating more visualizations both in similar theme to these, and also expanding to more texts. However, as a rising Senior in highschool, I am also quite busy for the next few months :)

projects.project_why:
My name is Shilo Sapir. I grew up in the United States, made Aliyah to Israel to serve in the IDF, and joined the Paratroopers brigade in a Haredi unit. During my service, I encountered a challenge many share — the deep desire to learn Torah, but the constant struggle to find time in a packed schedule. Over the years, I’ve realized this challenge extends far beyond soldiers to students, working parents, and people of all ages who want accessible, meaningful ways to bring Torah into their daily lives.

From this need, I developed Orayta — a smart app that uses AI technologies to help capitalize on free time slots in a personal calendar and allocate them to personalized Torah study, with direct links to high-quality content through Sefaria. The AI adapts to the user’s topic of interest, time available, and suggests a relevant source to learn so that the experience is tailored to both younger and older audiences — in language, design, and ease of use.

I believe that collaboration between Orayta and Sefaria can:

-Expand Sefaria’s user base to busy audiences of all ages, in Israel and worldwide.

-Increase engagement of existing users through an interactive, personalized learning experience.

-Signal innovation and openness to collaboration with grassroots entrepreneurs.

I would be happy to have a short conversation to present Orayta, demonstrate how the app works and integrates with Sefaria, share its marketing and outreach plan to new audiences, and explore possible business cooperation that would benefit both sides. Contact me in order to receive a one-pager and view an ad preview for the application.

Thank you for your time,

## What Is Mishneh AI
Mishneh AI (https://mishneh.ai) is an AI platform for studying Torah grounded in Jewish primary sources, not generic training data. Generic AI treats Jewish texts as one dataset among many, blends Torah with Wikipedia, hallucinates citations, and filters the sages through outside biases. We built Mishneh AI because we wanted to talk to Rambam, not a chatbot that once skimmed a summary of the Mishneh Torah. Every response draws from Torah, Talmud, Midrash, Halakhah, and rabbinic literature with citations users can verify on sefaria.org. Whether someone is a rabbi researching a topic or discovering the sages for the first time, the goal is to open the doors of the beit midrash to everyone.

The name is a nod to Rambam's great work. The Mishneh Torah was written with a radical goal: make the entire Oral Law accessible to anyone willing to learn. Mishneh AI carries that mission forward with modern technology, and Sefaria's open library is what makes it possible.

The platform has two AI study partners. Rambot is your researcher. Ask a question and he'll search the sources, synthesize what the tradition says, and cite every reference with numbered citations linking back to sefaria.org. Sifra is your chavruta. She's a conversational study partner who learns how you think, explores texts with you, and shares sources naturally like a friend across the table. Both are powered by the same retrieval engine but tuned for very different learning styles.

Mishneh AI also has a memory feature that learns what each user is interested in and investigating over time, so conversations get more relevant and personalized the more you use it. The roadmap is to keep expanding this with new discovery features and AI technologies to support learners of all types, from beginners looking for a starting point to scholars doing deep research.

## Project Description (Technical)

Under the hood, Mishneh AI runs a completely custom agentic RAG system built on Sefaria's open data. Multiple AI agents coordinate query classification, Hebrew/Aramaic query expansion, multi-stage vector search with cross-encoder reranking, and category diversity balancing across over 43,000 indexed passages in 14 categories of Jewish literature.

One feature I'm especially excited about is Primary Source Augmentation, which uses Sefaria's 3.7 million cross-text link records to trace citation chains back to the foundational Torah verses that secondary sources are based on. It's always climbing the tree to the roots. I also route different models to different tasks based on their strengths and have a memory feature that learns what each user is studying to personalize the experience over time.

I processed the full Sefaria-Export corpus (1,777 texts), parsed all 6,550 schema files for metadata enrichment, built a reverse index of 17,861 title aliases for transliteration resolution, and constructed a citation database from Sefaria's links CSVs. Every piece of the system is designed to keep users connected to the primary sources on sefaria.org.

projects.project_desc:
Derekh Learning is an AI-powered Jewish study companion that transforms any text from Sefaria into personalized lessons tailored to your knowledge level, interests, and available time. The app acts as an always-available chevruta (study partner), generating custom lessons from Torah portions, Talmud, Mishnah, or any Jewish text. Users choose a "learning path" that shapes how content is presented (Beginner, Intermediate, Expert, or custom perspectives like "Startup Founder"), select their text from daily learning cycles, and pick a lesson depth (Bite-Sized to Deep-Dive). The AI then creates comprehensive lessons with reflection prompts and study questions, all with embedded links directly back to the original sources on Sefaria for deeper exploration.
Beyond lesson generation, Derekh Learning serves as a complete Jewish learning toolkit: a Judaism 101 encyclopedia with a growing list of AI-generated entries on holidays and practices, an interactive Jewish calendar with one-tap lesson generation, location-based zmanim (prayer times), and a gematria calculator with spiritual insights. Every feature integrates deeply with Sefaria, lessons embed source links, the Commentary Explorer displays classical rabbis' interpretations from Sefaria's database, and the Hebrew dictionary pulls from Sefaria's lexicons. We don't replace Sefaria; we create an accessible entry point that helps beginners understand why a text matters and how to approach it, then guides them to Sefaria for authentic source study.

Torah Study Tracker A personal archive for your lifetime of Torah study. Powered by the Sefaria API, this app allows you to log your past learning, track repetitions, and build a visual library of everything you have studied. Alongside tools for managing your current daily routines, its primary goal is to give you a permanent, bird's-eye view of your learning journey and clearly map out what you have accomplished over the years.
